html:
The settlement of January 27 BCE in which Octavian handed his emergency powers back to the Senate and received them back in a new form, along with the name Augustus. It is the usual date for the start of the Roman Empire.

After Actium Octavian had sole control of the army and the state. On 13 January 27 BCE he announced that he was restoring the Republic. The Senate begged him to stay, gave him charge of the frontier provinces where most of the legions were, and on 16 January named him Augustus, "the revered one".

He called himself princeps, "first citizen", so this system is called the Principate. Elections, consuls and the Senate went on, but real power lay with him. In 23 BCE he gave up the consulship and took the powers of a tribune for life instead, and in 12 BCE he became pontifex maximus, head of the state religion.

The mask of the Republic fooled few, but after decades of civil war most Romans accepted it. It opened the Pax Romana and lasted, with changes, until the Crisis of the Third Century. See Augustus.
